transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi doctor. Well, what brings me in is that my head just feels really foggy lately. I'm a personal care aide, and I've been making these little mistakes in my client notes... and just forgetting what I was about to do. It's really not like me to be this scattered, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone.
Over what time period have you been noticing this fogginess and forgetfulness — has it been going on for days, weeks, or longer?
Well, I'd say it's been about a month now. This whole low, kind of guilty, foggy feeling has just been hanging over me for the last four weeks or so.
You mentioned feeling low and guilty — would you say your mood has been depressed or sad over this past month?
Yeah, I would say depressed. Lately, I just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I mean, I can still get through my shift and talk to people fine, but inside... I'm just sad and flat.
Have you had any recent illnesses, fever, infections, or changes in any medications you're taking in the past month or so?
No, I haven't had any of that. No fevers or infections, I haven't been sick at all. And I haven't had any changes to my medications, either. Everything physically has been pretty normal.
Over this past month, have you noticed that things you normally enjoy doing — like hobbies, time with friends, or activities you find fun — have stopped feeling enjoyable or interesting to you?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. I still watch my shows and catch up with friends when I can. It's just that I feel down while I'm doing them, but I wouldn't say I've lost interest or stopped enjoying them altogether.
Over this past month when you've been feeling down and foggy, have you also been experiencing worry, nervousness, or anxiety — either all day or most days?

No, I wouldn't say I've been anxious or worried. I mean, I have the usual stress, you know, paying bills and stuff, but nothing out of the ordinary. It's more just that heavy, sad feeling I mentioned, not really nervousness or anything like that.

When you think about this past month, would you say the foggy feeling in your head and the forgetfulness have been the main thing bothering you, or has the sad, heavy feeling in your chest been more of the core problem with the fogginess kind of coming along with it?

I think it's the sad feeling that's the main thing. Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. I mean, I can still get through my shift at work and talk to the clients and everything, but inside I just feel really sad and flat. The fogginess is there, but the heaviness is what's really weighing on me.
